core_goal: PCL-PGA block copolymer designed with hydrophobic PCL segments acting as hydrolysis barriers around degradable PGA blocks.
mechanism_one_liner: The semicrystalline PCL domains maintain mechanical coherence as PGA degrades
risk_one_liner: Phase separation may compromise mechanical homogeneity
pros_short: ['Well-understood block copolymer chemistry and degradation', 'Hydrophobic PCL segments effectively shield ester bonds']
cons_short: ['Risk of phase separation affecting mechanical homogeneity', 'Very slow degradation of PCL may hinder complete absorption']

core_goal: Combining permanent covalent crosslinks for stability with hydrolyzable ionic crosslinks that gradually break to control degradation rate while preserving integrity.
mechanism_one_liner: Covalent crosslinks maintain structural integrity throughout degradation
risk_one_liner: Ion leaching may cause local tissue inflammation
pros_short: ['Progressive degradation via labile ionic crosslinks preserves integrity', 'pH control mitigates autocatalytic degradation']
cons_short: ['Risk of ion leaching causing inflammation', 'Complex synthesis requiring precise stoichiometry']

core_goal: A core of slow-degrading high-crystallinity PLLA for structural support, coated with a fast-degrading PGA shell that delays water penetration to the core during early stages.
mechanism_one_liner: The crystalline PLLA core provides high initial stiffness and strength
risk_one_liner: Potential delamination under cyclic loading stresses
pros_short: ['Uses well-established, biocompatible polymers (PLLA, PGA)', 'Clear staged degradation mechanism']
cons_short: ['Delamination risk at core-shell interface under cyclic loading', 'Manufacturing complexity for uniform shell coating']
